title: 对亚洲母亲无所不能的刻板印象(2)
desc: 对亚洲母亲无所不能的刻板印象(2)

paragraphs.en: Given her ubiquity, leaving out the mother figure can be a statement in its own right.
paragraphs.zh: 母亲这一形象无处不在，因此，作品里刻意不写母亲，本身也成为一种表达。

paragraphs.en: In Cathy Park Hong's book Minor Feelings, Hong recalls a fellow poet once telling her: "You have an Asian mother. She has to be interesting."
paragraphs.zh: 凯茜·帕克·洪在《少数派的感受》一书中回忆，曾有另一位诗人对她说：“你有一位亚裔母亲。她一定很有故事。”

paragraphs.en: Hong refuses to engage: "I must defer, at least for now. I'd rather write about my friendship with Asian women first.
paragraphs.zh: 洪选择回避这个话题：“至少现在，我打算暂且搁置。我想先写我和亚裔女性之间的友谊。

paragraphs.en: My mother would take over, breaching the walls of these essays, until it is only her."
paragraphs.zh: 一旦写到母亲，她就会占据全部篇幅，冲破这些散文的边界，整篇文字只剩下她。”

paragraphs.en: Perhaps she has a point.
paragraphs.zh: 或许她说得有道理。

paragraphs.en: In these stories, the mother has a way of growing impossibly large; she becomes the device through which questions of immigration, identity and history are explored.
paragraphs.zh: 在这些故事里，母亲的形象会变得无比庞大；她成为载体，借由她，作者探讨移民、身份与历史议题。

paragraphs.en: It is in the conflict between the mother and daughter that we come to see the cultural clashes between east and west.
paragraphs.zh: 正是在母女冲突之中，我们得以看见东西方之间的文化碰撞。

paragraphs.en: These stories thrum with the pain of mutual unintelligibility between the first-generation immigrant who has known hunger and suffering and the second-generation child who craves love.
paragraphs.zh: 这些故事，回荡着两代人互不理解带来的痛苦：饱经饥饿苦难的第一代移民，与渴求爱意的第二代子女，彼此无法读懂对方。

paragraphs.en: The standoff seems intractable.
paragraphs.zh: 这种对峙看似无解。

paragraphs.en: In sentimental Hollywood fare, these figures end up enjoying a cathartic reconciliation.
paragraphs.zh: 在温情的好莱坞影片里，人物最终会达成宣泄式的和解。

paragraphs.en: In more highbrow works, the child reaches for some kind of resolution through their art, protected by the fact that the mother cannot understand English or has died.
paragraphs.zh: 在更严肃的文学作品中，子女借助艺术找到某种和解方式，这份慰藉来自一个现实：母亲不懂英文，或是已经离世。

paragraphs.en: Over drinks in London one evening last summer, I mentioned to some old schoolfriends that I was thinking of writing about the persistent trope of the Asian mother.
paragraphs.zh: 去年夏天一个夜晚，我在伦敦和几位老同学小酌，提起我打算写写反复出现的亚裔母亲这一文学母题。

paragraphs.en: Polite small talk was swiftly done away with, followed by two hours of impassioned discussion.
paragraphs.zh: 客套闲聊很快结束，随后我们热烈讨论了两个小时。

paragraphs.en: Afterwards, I wanted to find a way into this subject that I was now beginning to see everywhere.
paragraphs.zh: 那次交谈之后，我希望找到一个切入点，这个主题如今在各处都能看到。

paragraphs.en: The subject was too vast to be treated definitively, so I started closer to home.
paragraphs.zh: 这个议题太过宏大，无法一次性彻底讲透，于是我从身边入手。

paragraphs.en: Taking a highly unscientific and piecemeal approach, I asked my friends if they could speak to me at greater length about their relationship with their mothers.
paragraphs.zh: 我采用很不系统、零散的方式，请朋友们和我深入聊聊她们和母亲的关系。

paragraphs.en: It is true that no matter which continent they are from, mothers are the inexhaustible subject: the inevitable endpoint of a therapy session, the proverbial container of infinite grievances, the shortcut to understanding a person's idiosyncrasies and insecurities.
paragraphs.zh: 诚然，无论来自哪个大陆，母亲永远是写不尽的主题：心理治疗谈话绕不开的终点，承载无尽委屈的代名词，读懂一个人怪癖与不安的捷径。

paragraphs.en: But there is something about the Asian mother in popular culture that feels both overexposed and underdeveloped.
paragraphs.zh: 但流行文化中的亚裔母亲形象，有种奇特的矛盾：曝光度极高，刻画却又浅薄不足。

paragraphs.en: What is behind this constant return to the mother figure in literature and cinema and in our own lives?
paragraphs.zh: 为什么文学、电影，还有我们自己的生活里，总会反复回到母亲这个形象？

paragraphs.en: When we write about her flaws and failures, and our disappointments and broken inheritances, what exactly are we looking at?
paragraphs.zh: 当我们书写她的缺点与失败，书写我们的失望与破碎的家族传承，我们究竟在审视什么？

paragraphs.en: And what are we hoping to find?
paragraphs.zh: 又希望从中找到什么？

paragraphs.en: Anecessary disclaimer: not every Asian mother fits the stereotype and not every Asian mother-daughter relationship is complicated and fraught. (Ours is an age of hedging.)
paragraphs.zh: 在此需要必要说明：并非所有亚裔母亲都符合这套刻板印象，也不是所有亚裔母女关系都充满矛盾与痛苦。（这是一个凡事需要预留余地的时代。）

paragraphs.en: My friend Min claims to have identified three types of mother-child relationships.
paragraphs.zh: 我的朋友敏说，她把亲子关系分成三类。

paragraphs.en: "The first, which I don't understand, is people who are friends with their mums and tell their mums everything."
paragraphs.zh: “第一种，我无法理解：孩子和母亲像朋友，什么话都告诉妈妈。”

paragraphs.en: The second group are children "who have conflict with their parents, but they're normal conflicts".
paragraphs.zh: 第二类是孩子“和父母有矛盾，但只是普通的争执”。

paragraphs.en: And then, she says, "there's this third group, where you have conflict, but it reaches far beyond the conflict, and it's very hard to explain to somebody who's never experienced it".
paragraphs.zh: 而第三类，她说：“同样存在冲突，但矛盾远远超出普通争吵，没经历过的人很难解释清楚。”

paragraphs.en: Min's mother, she told me, "is able to make me feel worthless, useless, terrible, ungrateful; that she's wasted her life on you, and you are the worst person in the world, and you'll never amount to anything."
paragraphs.zh: 敏告诉我，她的母亲“总能让我觉得自己一无是处、毫无用处、糟糕透顶、忘恩负义；仿佛她为你耗尽一生，而你是世上最差劲的人，永远不会有出息。”

paragraphs.en: Min and I went to a competitive international school in Hong Kong, the kind that attracts status-conscious middle- and upper-class parents with high hopes for their children.
paragraphs.zh: 我和敏曾在香港一所竞争激烈的国际学校就读，这所学校吸引的是看重社会地位、对子女寄予厚望的中产与上层家庭。

paragraphs.en: To illustrate: one of my friends' mums would regularly call another school mum to gossip about the grades of everyone in our year (it was rumoured that they had a source on the inside, a Mandarin-language teacher).
paragraphs.zh: 举个例子：我一位朋友的妈妈会经常打电话给另一位同学的母亲，打探我们年级所有人的成绩（传闻她们在校内有线人，一位中文老师）。

paragraphs.en: Our teenage years were spent anxiously tracking the rise and fall of our competition.
paragraphs.zh: 少年时代的我们，焦虑地盯着同龄竞争者成绩的起落。

paragraphs.en: Any failures on our part were borne alone, in secret shame.
paragraphs.zh: 我们所有的失败，都只能独自承受，藏在心底，满怀羞耻。

paragraphs.en: By my late teens, I began to feel that something wasn't right.
paragraphs.zh: 十八九岁的时候，我慢慢感觉到哪里不对劲。

paragraphs.en: I had got the impression from American films and TV that your teenage years should be a time of self-discovery; of making mistakes, figuring out who you are, and doing keg stands on California beaches.
paragraphs.zh: 美国影视剧给我的印象是，少年时代本该是自我探索的时期：犯错，找到自我，在加州海滩玩啤酒桶游戏。

paragraphs.en: But in my world, life wasn't about that.
paragraphs.zh: 但在我的世界里，生活并非如此。

paragraphs.en: As one classmate opined in the year 13 common room: life was about survival.
paragraphs.zh: 一位同学在十二年级公共休息室这样评价：生活就是生存。

paragraphs.en: Study hard, excel in school and get a high-paying job you don't enjoy so you can support the family you will need to have.
paragraphs.zh: 努力读书、学业拔尖，找一份自己并不喜欢的高薪工作，供养你未来要组建的家庭。

paragraphs.en: Make sure to have plenty of children.
paragraphs.zh: 还要生很多孩子。
